claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CEO Ted Pick said investments in the self-directed and Workplace channels "drive our differentiated client acquisition funnel." He said the expanded offering reaches over 19 million relationships and that the firm added net new assets of over $250 billion in each of the past two years, "on track to delivering $10 trillion plus of total client assets."

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), Ted Pick said ongoing investments in the platform, "including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel," serve as an engine for future growth.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Ted Pick said the financial advisor workplace and E*TRADE retail channels are each thriving. He said the firm attracted $1.6 trillion plus of net new assets over the last five years and concluded "The funnel is working."

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya credited "sustained investments in our client acquisition funnel" with letting the firm reach more clients and deepen existing relationships. She said advisers, a culture of innovation and unique capabilities are the foundation of the business, and that the connectivity of the Integrated Firm sets it apart.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Sharon Yeshaya said that since acquiring E*TRADE and expanding the workplace offering 6 years ago the firm has added over $2 trillion of net new assets. She described this as a differentiated client acquisition funnel and said scale supports continued investment in technology, including AI and digital tools.

Workplace as a feeder - 3Q25 call (October 2025): management said assets that originated from workplace continue to migrate into the advisor-led channel because of consistent platform investment. It said the reopening of the IPO market showed the workplace channel is "a powerful asset acquisition tool." On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), the CFO said advisor-led flows were particularly strong, from new advisors attracted to the strength of the workplace and from assets that originated from workplace.

Advisor-led flows from Workplace and E*TRADE, and the Integrated Firm - 4Q25 call (January 2026): management said advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships grew to a record $99 billion for the full year, against historical averages of around $60 billion per year. It said 4Q25 net new assets of $122 billion had contributions across all channels, with growth supported by institutional relationships related to the integrated firm.

Workplace retention and migration - 1Q26 call (April 2026): the CFO said Workplace stood out as having sourced clients who continue to aggregate assets onto the platform and benefit from stock plan vesting events. She cited greater retention of vested assets, which translated into net new assets. She also described channel migration, in which workplace assets seek advice, as contributing to over $1 trillion of total assets in the adviser-led strategy.

IPO flows and referrals from Institutional Securities - 2Q26 (July 2026): Ted Pick said Morgan Stanley connected the Integrated Firm to "translate institutional strength into client value through our adviser-led and E*TRADE channels." He said the record $148 billion of net new assets was driven by large IPOs of late-stage private workplace clients. The CFO said stock plan IPO flows were just over half of NNA and showed the workplace channel as a contributor to "the top of the funnel."

3Q26 call (October 2026): the CFO said the $232 billion of net new assets reflected the core business and "differentiated growth opportunities created by Workplace and the integrated firm." She said IPO-related flows again contributed just over half of NNA. She said the pipeline and connectivity across channels let the firm "build relationships early and deepen them over time."

Advisor recruiting and attraction: on the 1Q25 call (April 2025), the CFO said NNA was supported by advisor-led client flows, stock plan vesting events, "positive recruiting trends" and self-directed clients. The 10-K and 10-Q list "our ability to attract and retain financial advisors and clients" among the factors that influence the level of NNA.
claims.source_label: MS transcript 2025-03-31 [IR]; MS 10-K - Wealth Management segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Channel scale data in the 3Q26 supplement (published October 2026): self-directed households were 8.8 million and self-directed client assets $1,802 billion. Stock plan unvested public assets were $638 billion and advisor-led client assets $6,631 billion.
claims.source_label: MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30, p.8 [IR]

claims.text: Results, oldest to newest. The 4Q24 call (January 2025) said full-year 2024 NNA of $252 billion represented approximately 5% annual growth of beginning period assets. The 1Q25 call (April 2025) gave NNA of $94 billion, "representing a 6% annualized growth rate of beginning period assets." The 2Q25 call (July 2025) gave NNA of $59 billion, inclusive of a $22 billion headwind from tax outflows.
claims.source_label: MS transcript 2024-12-31 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-03-31 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: The 10-K for 2025 (published February 2026) reports Wealth Management net new assets of $356 billion and fee-based asset flows of $160 billion for 2025. Quarterly NNA in the supplements was $81.0 billion in 3Q25 and $122.3 billion in 4Q25. It was then $118.4 billion in 1Q26, $148.1 billion in 2Q26 and $232.4 billion in 3Q26, against $81.0 billion in 3Q25.
claims.source_label: MS 10-K 2025-12-31 [filing]; MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30, p.8 [IR]; MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-03-31, p.8 [IR]; MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30, p.8 [IR]

claims.text: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), the CFO said no single driver stood out in the $118 billion quarter. She cited high engagement across the adviser-led platform and said Workplace is "becoming a bigger and bigger contributor."

In 2Q26 and 3Q26, management and filings say just over half of NNA came from IPO-related inflows in the Workplace channel. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said roughly $0.5 trillion of NNA and about $175 billion of fee-based flows had been delivered in the first 9 months of the year.
claims.source_label: MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]; MS press - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30 [filing]; MS transcript 2026-09-30 [IR]

claims.text: Stated target: on the 1Q26 call (April 2026), management said total client assets across Wealth and Investment Management exceed $9 trillion "on the road to $10 trillion plus." The January 2026 strategic update deck states that attainment of its objectives "assumes a normal market environment." On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Ted Pick said "this is not the time to overreach."
claims.source_label: MS transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]; MS deck 2026-01-15, p.18 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]

claims.text: Headwinds the firm names: the 10-K for 2025 (February 2026) says the level of NNA is influenced by factors including client investment and spending behaviors, seasonality, advisor and client attraction and retention, capital market and corporate activities, and "large idiosyncratic inflows and outflows." It adds that, "Should these factors continue, the growth rate of our NNA may be impacted." The 10-Q for 2Q26 (August 2026) repeats this language and notes that just over half of the quarter's $148 billion was IPO-related Workplace inflows.
claims.source_label: MS 10-K - Wealth Management segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: The 10-K risk factors (February 2026) say unfavorable market or economic conditions can affect investor confidence and the level and mix of client assets, including deposits. It says this "could also impact the level of net new asset flows and/or flows into fee-based assets," and that this could negatively affect Wealth Management results.

3Q26 call (October 2026): the CFO said "flows will fluctuate as lockups expire, funds make distributions and individuals use assets for consumption." She also said net interest income was down modestly as deposits grew and the mix shifted, and that the expected modest 4Q increase is "subject to rates and client behavior."

Competition: the 10-K (February 2026) says Morgan Stanley competes with commercial banks, global investment banks, regional banks, broker-dealers, private banks, registered investment advisers, digital investing platforms, asset managers and fintech firms. The 10-Q for 1Q26 (May 2026) says the level of interest rates may affect deposits held at the Firm "given competition for deposits from other institutions and alternative cash-equivalent products."

Deposits and cash management: the supplements show Wealth Management deposits of $465 billion at September 30, 2026 against $398 billion a year earlier. The period-end annualized weighted average cost of deposits was 2.85% against 2.72%. The 10-Q for 2Q26 shows the cash management average fee rate at 5 bps against 6 bps a year earlier.
claims.source_label: MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30, p.8 [IR]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Positioning (affiliation options): The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options, which it calls AdvisorChoice, with advisors affiliating as employees, independent contractors, or through its RIA and Custody Services division. The firm says its ability to attract advisors rests on its values-based culture, its commitment to service and the unique ways it serves advisors.

Positioning (website, page content as of 2026-04-21): The recruiting page describes AdvisorChoice as five options: Traditional Employee (with book ownership), Advisor Select (lead your own branch), Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA. The page also lists RIA & Custody Services. It says all are backed by a leading independent financial firm.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Positioning (employee-channel pitch, pages as of 2026-05-16 and 2026-03-11): The Traditional Employee page promises advisor book ownership and says advisors are free to succeed 'no quotas, no product pushing'. The Advisor Select page offers established advisors employee-channel benefits with the independence to build their own branch and 'earn a higher rate on production'.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-05-16 [IR]; RJF press page content as of 2026-03-11 [IR]

claims.text: Positioning (calls, July 2025 to January 2026): Management described a 'best of both worlds' value proposition on the call published 2025-07-23, and repeated it on the calls published 2025-10-22 and 2026-01-28. It combines an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions. Management said its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence are a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives, and that it keeps investing in its platform. Examples cited were the private wealth advisor program, an expanded alternatives platform and a proprietary AI operations agent called Rai.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2025-06-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-09-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]

claims.text: Positioning (wirehouses and others, call published 2026-01-28): CEO Paul Shoukry said advisors are coming 'from wires, regionals, other independents', and that it is not one firm driving the success. He said Raymond James has 'the largest addressable market across our affiliation options', from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, with critical mass and decades of experience in each.

Positioning (calls published 2026-04-22 and 2026-07-22): Management said its client-first culture, technology and product platforms and strong balance sheet make Raymond James a 'destination of choice' for advisors across its affiliation options. In July 2026 Shoukry said 'advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities'. He cited a 97% adviser satisfaction rate and said the firm is 'agnostic' about how an adviser affiliates. He also said the firm invests $1.1 billion in technology and that smaller firms 'can't keep up' with that level of investment.

Positioning (independent contractor and RIA pitch): The independent contractor page (as of 2026-05-19) says the firm offers a 'partnership in independence'. It describes a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer, with private wealth, technology and marketing support. The RIA & Custody Services page (as of 2026-07-12) says it offers control 'free from retail conflict', plus transitions management and recruiting assistance. The 10-K says independent contractors bear their direct costs and receive a higher payout percentage than employee advisors.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-05-19 [IR]; RJF press page content as of 2026-07-12 [IR]; RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]

claims.text: Recruiting results (FY2025, call published 2025-10-22): Management reported record recruiting to the domestic independent contractor and employee channels. Trailing-12-month production at the advisors' previous firms totaled $407 million, a 21% increase over the prior record, with approximately $58 billion of client assets at their previous firms. Including assets recruited into RIA and Custody Services, total recruited client assets over the past 12 months were nearly $63 billion. Management also reported a record 8,943 financial advisors, and said the pipeline and commitments to join in coming quarters were strong.

Headcount (FY2025 10-K, published 2025-11-25): The firm had 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2025. The 10-K says the count rose because new recruits and trainees moved into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements. RCS-division advisors are not counted in the financial advisor metric.

Recruiting results (call published 2026-04-22): For the quarter, recruited advisors had trailing-12-month production of $141 million and nearly $21 billion of client assets at their previous firms. Management called this the second-highest quarterly result in the firm's history for both recruited production and assets.

Recruiting results (call published 2026-07-22): For the quarter, recruited advisors had trailing-12-month production of $156 million and nearly $23 billion of client assets at their previous firms. Through the first nine months of the fiscal year, recruited production was $393 million with more than $56 billion of client assets. Management said this puts the firm 'on a clear path to exceed the record results set in fiscal 2025'.

Pipeline (call published 2026-07-22): Shoukry said the recruiting pipeline 'remains diverse across our affiliation options'. He said it is 'not a pipeline that is driven by one firm or one catalyst' and that management does not think it is idiosyncratic. The July 22, 2026 press release cites 'robust financial advisor recruiting'.

Mix of recruiting (call published 2026-04-22): Shoukry said that over the last year much more recruiting has come from the independent side than the employee side. This shifts the payout mix toward independents, whose payouts are higher because they cover their own overhead.

Payout ranges (recruiting page, page content as of 2026-04-21): Raymond James lists Traditional Employee at 'Up to 50% payout' plus employee benefits, with a minimum of 5 years of experience. Advisor Select is listed at 70-80% gross payout, with a minimum of 3 years of experience and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue. Independent Contractor is listed at 81% to 90% payout, with minimum 3 years of experience and a minimum T12 of $150,000 to join an existing branch or $400,000 to open a new one. Corporate RIA is listed at 81% to 90% payout.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Bank & Credit Union (recruiting page, as of 2026-04-21): The page says advisors receive 'a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James' during the transition. The qualification listed is a minimum of 3 years of experience and $250,000 in production. A related page (as of 2026-05-17) describes institutions offering 'attractive and competitive recruiting deals'.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]; RJF press page content as of 2026-05-17 [IR]

claims.text: Deal philosophy (calls published 2026-01-28 and 2026-07-22): Shoukry said 'We have to have a competitive check', but the firm wants advisors who want to be there long term and does not target advisors moving 'for the highest check'. In July 2026 he said: 'we don't lead with the highest check... we lead with culture and capabilities', and that the firm has 'always been disciplined' on transition assistance economics.

Transition assistance structure (calls published 2026-01-28 and 2026-04-22): Management said it prefers recruiting advisors one by one rather than through acquisitions. Its reason is that '100% of the transition assistance' goes to retention of the advisor rather than to a seller, and that it can ensure cultural fit. Management said annual recruiting is now comparable to a medium-sized acquisition, which is why it broke out recruiting and retention cost.

Mechanics of incentives (filings): Recruiting and retention-related compensation includes cash and equity awards issued in conjunction with recruiting activities, expensed over the requisite service period (typically between 5 and 10 years). The firm also offers loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting and retention, and the 10-Q published 2026-05-06 reports that 'Loans to financial advisors, net' increased $268 million due to recruiting and retention-related activity. The 10-Q published 2026-02-06 and other 10-Q/MD&A chunks cite higher financial advisor recruiting-related expenses.
claims.source_label: RJF supplement 2026-06-30, p.18 [IR]; RJF 10-Q 2025-06-30 [filing]; RJF 10-Q 2026-03-31 [filing]; RJF 10-Q 2025-12-31 [filing]

claims.text: Competitive environment (FY2025 10-K, published 2025-11-25): The firm describes a 'highly competitive recruiting environment' driven by an industry-wide trend of advisors leaving traditional firms, including for independent RIAs, some backed by private equity. It notes that other firms offer guaranteed contracts, upfront payments and increased compensation, and that its own results may be hurt by the cost of loans or incentives to recruits. It participates in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting but notes competitors may withdraw. It also notes it has faced unfair-hiring claims and may face more.

Competitors (calls published 2025-07-23 and 2025-10-22): Shoukry said the environment 'remains competitive' and that the relatively new factor is PE-backed roll-ups, which have been 'extremely aggressive' in paying higher multiples. In October 2025 he said there are 'still very rich deals out there from the roll-ups and aggregators'. He said competitors 'compete with the largest check', and that many are looking for an exit in three to five years or change comp plans every year to cross-sell bank products.

Competitors and Raymond James's stance (calls published 2026-01-28 to 2026-07-22): In January 2026 Shoukry said competitive pressure is higher with PE-backed roll-ups, and that firms talking about leaning in to recruiting 'next quarter' is 'not sustainable'. In April 2026 he said valuations of those firms would be closely watched, and that Raymond James retained advisors well 'despite the very competitive environment'. In July 2026 he said recruiting cannot be turned on and off quarter to quarter and that the firm wants consistency.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Limits and losses the firm names: The 10-K says domestic PCG net new assets were negatively affected by the departure of primarily one large branch in the independent contractor division in the first fiscal quarter of 2025. On the call published 2025-01-29, management put the impact at approximately $5 billion of AUA. On the call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry also flagged a platform of about $2.7 billion that would be lost to bank M&A.

Wirehouse-sourced recruits (trade press, indicative only): Trade press published 2026-11-05 reported that Raymond James brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley with combined assets exceeding $1 billion, and a $420 million Edward Jones team in Virginia. A report published 2026-09-02 described a team that previously managed more than $550 million at UBS Financial Services. A report published 2026-11-12 described a team of about $700 million from Truist Investment Services joining through the Financial Institutions Division (FID).
claims.source_label: RJF trade 2026-11-05 [trade press (indicative only)]; RJF trade 2026-09-02 [trade press (indicative only)]; RJF trade 2026-11-12 [trade press (indicative only)]

claims.text: Trade press (InvestmentNews, 2026-11-03, indicative only) reports that Schwab invested in Nevis' $70 million Series B; Nevis aims to have AI agents open accounts and handle other operations for RIAs on Schwab's custody platform. The same report says Schwab's Claude for Financial Advisors setup is limited to read-only access.

Trade press (InvestmentNews, 2026-10-29, indicative only) cites recent RIA launches with Schwab custody: an advisory duo that managed about $18.6 billion at J.P. Morgan Advisors launched Latigo Peak Partners with custodians Schwab and BNY Pershing. Last year a $129 billion team left Merrill Lynch for OpenArc Corporate Advisory, an RIA on the Dynasty Financial Network with custody at Schwab.

Trade press (2026-10-29) quotes Wurster saying "the pipeline is robust" for more advisors to move to the RIA space. He said Schwab has tried to make the path to independence as easy as possible, by investing in its own process and working with partners such as Dynasty.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-28, indicative only) reports that Wurster told advisors at Schwab Impact that Schwab will continue to focus on custody for RIAs with under $100 million. He described Schwab's job as providing a platform and support ecosystem that helps advisors support their clients and thrive.

The same trade report (2026-10-28) says Fidelity, the second-largest custodian, told RIAs in early October that firms with under $100 million in client assets must leave its platform by June 30, 2027. It adds that Schwab and other custodians are seeking to appeal to advisors who may be looking for a new custodian.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-28, indicative only) reports that Schwab made Claude for Financial Advisors available through its Schwab Advisor Center. RIAs can sign up for an enterprise license with a 20-seat minimum, or a smaller-teams option that requires meeting security measures. Advisors who sign up by Nov. 30 get a $4,800 credit, equal to a 12-month 20-seat minimum, which Schwab's head of AI for Advisor Services said is meant to offset the cost for smaller RIAs.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-23, indicative only) reports that Syntax integrated its Syntax Direct index engine with Schwab Advisor Services' iRebal rebalancing platform. RIAs access it through single sign-on, and custom indices flow into iRebal through an API as model portfolios.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (published 2026-10-15), Wurster described the adviser business as built around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed. Schwab serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets, with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending, technology, and dedicated service and support. He said Schwab is continuing to invest in the business.

On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-15), Wurster said more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as a custodian last year, more than 3x the number of the next closest provider. The 3Q26 deck shows custodians added to ADVs of 1,101 for Schwab versus 349, 339, 202 and 79 for Peers A to D. The peers are not named.

On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-15), Wurster said the long/short program helped drive some Advisor Services NNA and some consolidation to Schwab. Schwab changed the long/short minimums in October and throttled growth to some extent. He said Advisor Services NNA growth has "in no way slowed" and that Client Promoter Scores, intent to bring new assets, and ease of doing business among advisers are at their highest. This is management's characterization.

The 3Q26 press release (2026-10-15) reports margin loan balances of $187.9 billion at quarter-end, including $60.7 billion related to long/short strategies. It also says Schwab partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors to the independent RIAs it serves. The 3Q26 call has Wurster saying Schwab is the first RIA custodian included in it.

Trade press (2026-10-15, indicative only) reports that Wurster said Schwab is working on a proprietary long-short investment strategy and will update soon. The same report says Schwab and Fidelity have recently limited long-short strategies to manage high demand. Wurster is quoted saying Schwab can run the product efficiently from a balance sheet and operational standpoint.
On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-15), Wurster said Schwab is #1 by RIA custodial assets, as well as #1 by total client assets and #1 in daily average trades. The 3Q26 deck shows "#1 RIA Custodial Assets".

Trade press (RIABiz, 2026-09-23, indicative only) lists recent Schwab custody wins from Ameriprise's channel. These include breakaway StackStone Wealth ($1.9 billion AUA) in June, Fathom Advisors ($1.3 billion AUA) in September, and Seven Bridges Wealth Advisors (about $1 billion AUA), which joined the NewEdge Advisors rollup with Schwab as a core custodian.

The August 2026 Monthly Activity Report (published 2026-09-15) shows Advisor Services assets receiving ongoing advisory services at 5,903.0 at August month-end, up 21% year over year. The prior month-end figure was 5,763.1.

Trade press (2026-08-26, indicative only) quotes consultant Besheer saying Vanguard's move to position itself as an RIA custodian and technology platform provider, with Altruist, "clearly sets them up to compete with Fidelity for sure, and arguably it sets them up competitively with Schwab." Vanguard's spokesperson spoke about serving investors who work with RIAs and did not comment on that thesis.

Trade press (InvestmentNews, 2026-08-24, indicative only) reports Schwab raised the Schwab Advisor Network referral minimum to $5 million. A Schwab spokesperson said more than half of SAN's net flows come from clients with $10 million or more, and that Schwab remains committed to SAN. The report names Fidelity's Wealth Advisor Solutions as the competing referral program. One consultant quoted suggests advisors on both channels may be reallocating to Fidelity. Goldman Sachs and TradePMR by Robinhood have also debuted referral programs.

On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-21), Wurster said Schwab is the "natural leader in the adviser space" and expects more than 5% NNA growth there. He said it has been 6% plus in that business over the last four quarters or so. Separately, he said Schwab is investing in the build-out of an RIA support ecosystem.

The 2Q26 deck (2026-07-21) shows RIA custodial assets of $5.7T, ranked #1. The 2Q26 press release says long/short strategy interest remained strong among RIA clients, with margin loan debits of $42.1 billion and short cash credits of $43.7 billion as of June 30, 2026.

On the 2Q26 call (2026-07-21), Wurster said RIAs value Schwab's bank because they do not have to introduce another relationship to their clients. The 1H26 deck lists "Structured Asset Line" and "Advisor UHNW Services" among select highlights.

The May 2026 Investor Day deck (published 2026-05-14) states Schwab's aim to be "the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service." It also lists "Broaden support for RIAs while improving monetization" under growth.
claims.source_label: SCHW deck 2026-05-14, p.23 [IR]; SCHW deck 2026-05-14, p.25 [IR]

claims.text: The Investor Day deck (2026-05-14) says that with over $5T in assets Schwab leads the RIA channel, which it expects to exceed wirehouse channel assets. It shows the RIA channel as the fastest-growing advised category and cites a Schwab market share on that chart.

On the 1Q26 call (published 2026-04-16), Wurster said Schwab continues to invest to make it easier for advisers to do business with it, and has added lending capabilities. He cited a recently launched structured asset lending program, letting clients borrow against alternative investments and restricted or private shares so advisers keep the wealth relationship. He also described digital enhancements across RIA workflows (move money, account open, account maintenance) and modernized tools on the adviser platform.

On the 1Q26 call (2026-04-16), CFO Verdeschi said Schwab's model is informed by investors' preferences for lower explicit fees without sacrificing product access, convenience or service. He said Schwab has flexibility to keep supporting investors and RIAs as they expect if those preferences change.

The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says that in the Advisor Services arena Schwab competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

The 2025 10-K (2026-02-25) describes Advisor Services as providing custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs. Management says it can maintain its competitive position through its sales, support, technology and business consulting teams, with a scalable platform for administering clients' assets.

The 2025 10-K (2026-02-25) describes the RIA platform. The Advisor Services website covers account opening, money movement, transfers, and trading, with third-party integrations. Schwab Advisor Portfolio Connect is free to advisors, and thinkpipes and iRebal handle trading and rebalancing. It states that as custodian Schwab earns revenue predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees, and does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.

On the 4Q25 call (published 2026-01-21), Wurster said "we're winning across every dimension" in Advisor Services, citing size, scale, custody offering, consulting and support for independence, and product capabilities. He said Schwab grew that business roughly 6.5% organically in 2025. This is management's characterization.

On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-21), Wurster said Pledged Asset Line penetration reached 23% with 85% growth in originations in the last year. He said wirehouses are doing a better job of leveraging banking capabilities, that RIAs want to match that, and that Schwab is the natural provider.

On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-21), Wurster said Advisor Services launched Advisor ProDirect, a subscription service supporting RIAs, and nearly doubled its institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform.

On the 3Q25 call (published 2025-10-16), Wurster said Schwab is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody. He cited lending support, alternatives capability, an institutional no-transaction fee mutual fund platform with funds from nearly 60 managers, and Advisor ProDirect for breakaway advisors.

adjacent.text: On the 3Q26 call and press release (published 2026-10-15), core net new assets totaled $190.4 billion, up 38% versus 3Q25, an annualized growth rate of 5.8%. Schwab Wealth Advisory net flows grew 55% versus 3Q25 (per the release header).
adjacent.differs_because: These are firm-wide figures (and a retail wealth offer), not Advisor Services or RIA-only NNA.

adjacent.text: Under the 2023 IDA agreement (10-Q for 3Q25, published 2025-11-07), uninvested cash within eligible brokerage client accounts is swept off-balance sheet to the TD Depository Institutions, with a 15 basis point service fee. IDA balances must stay between a $60 billion minimum and $90 billion maximum.
adjacent.differs_because: This describes the firm-wide sweep arrangement for eligible brokerage accounts. It does not state RIA-specific sweep terms or pricing.

gaps.what: Schwab does not say in its own filings or calls that it is losing ground in RIA custody. Management's statements describe strength, and the evidence on pullbacks (the long/short minimum change and the SAN referral minimum increase) comes from the 3Q26 call and trade press.

gaps.what: A dollar figure for Advisor Services net new assets or RIA flows is not given in the evidence. Management cites only percentage organic growth (6% plus over the last four quarters, per the 2Q26 call) and firm-wide core NNA.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab Advisor Services segment disclosures in the 10-Q/10-K, or Advisor Services NNA slides in the quarterly earnings deck

gaps.what: RIA-specific cash sweep or bank sweep terms and any advisor-services pricing beyond 'no custody fee' are not found in the evidence provided. The IDA sweep agreement covers eligible brokerage accounts firm-wide.

claims.text: Strategy change, per trade press: AdvisorHub (2026-11-16) reports that Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting. It says the firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 and returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. (Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.)

Competition for advisors, per trade press: AdvisorHub (2026-11-16) reports Merrill recruiting wins from UBS (a Denver advisor managing $375 million), from Morgan Stanley (an advisor managing $205 million in California) and from Edward D. Jones & Co. (an advisor overseeing $150 million in Texas). It also reports that UBS executives said recruiting and retention were returning to historical norms after at least 27 teams overseeing $28 billion combined left in the first half of this year.
Competition for advisors, per trade press: AdvisorHub (2026-11-16) reports a private wealth team managing $1 billion in assets moved from UBS Wealth Management USA to Merrill in Boston.

Where Merrill is losing advisors, per trade press: InvestmentNews (2026-11-12) reports a Merrill financial solutions advisor joined an independent RIA, Trinity Wealth Advisors. It says that in March 2026 Cyndeo Wealth Partners added a Merrill veteran with roughly $235 million in client assets, one of several similar transitions in the industry this year where advisors cite greater autonomy and mission alignment.

Where Merrill is losing advisors, per trade press: WealthManagement.com (2026-11-03) reports JPMorgan recruited Tiffany Yu, managing about $940 million, from Merrill (registered with Merrill since 1998). It also reports J.P. Morgan Wealth appointed another Merrill alum, Linda Patel, as Southeast Regional Director.

Training and recruiting offer, in Merrill's own recruiting pages (page content as of 2026-11-03): the Advisor Development Program offers industry-leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses, a base salary and unlimited earning potential, high-quality leads and coaching by a dedicated leadership team. Path A (Client Associate) takes about 13 months including three months of licensing, Path B (Financial Solutions Advisor) about 13 months, and the ADP Financial Advisor stage about 1-4 years, after which people graduate to Merrill Core Advisor. The experienced-advisor page pitches the brand, lead generation through Bank of America's global bank and trust division, and access to Merrill's wealth platform and Bank of America's banking and trust capabilities.

claims.text: On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CEO Ted Pick cited ongoing investments in Morgan Stanley's platform, "including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel," as an engine for future growth.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said early AI use cases, some live and some in pilot, are showing progress. She named DevGen AI (developer efficiency), Parable (an interactive tool that analyzes and summarizes data), and LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors.

On the same 3Q25 call (October 2025), the CFO said the firm continues to invest to deepen its competitive moats, citing an expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and digital-asset partnerships with Zero Hash.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Ted Pick said the firm continues to invest in each of its three segments, including Wealth, "via human capital and technology," and that its growth plans embed increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside its client base. He said confidence is rising in the potential for AI to bring efficiency and effectiveness.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Pick described early work on digital assets in wealth, saying the firm is looking to expand capabilities after the Zero Hash partnership. He also described continued work on E*TRADE to keep the platform interesting for its active self-directed community. He said that even with ongoing investments in AI in core technology and AI efficiency and effectiveness tools, the firm expects to keep realizing operating leverage if markets are constructive and it executes.

The 2025 10-K (published February 2026) states that, in Wealth Management, the firm's ability to compete across advisor-led, workplace and digital direct channels is affected by multiple factors, including "our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization."

On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Pick said the "arms race of one AI platform versus another" is not new and that the firm considers it additive to what it has: world-class technology, world-class cyber defense and trusted advisers. He called the trusted adviser, including the wealth management financial adviser, "the key."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), the CFO said higher technology-driven spend relates to investments to support infrastructure, AI-enabled efficiencies and ongoing business growth. She also said Wealth Management's 30.5% pretax margin reflects the scale of the business and "the intentional strategic investments for our future."

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), the CFO said the firm continues to invest across its technology stack, "embracing AI tools to support our infrastructure, business growth and people." She also said the firm's scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools.

gaps.what: No dollar amount or budget for technology spending directed at financial advisors specifically was found in the evidence. Management describes technology investment only in general terms, covering the enterprise, the technology stack and AI tools. The evidence also names no advisor-facing AI tool beyond LeadIQ, which is described as lead distribution.

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options it calls AdvisorChoice. Advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division. The firm describes employee advisors as working in a traditional branch with local management and admin staff, serving predominantly retail clients, and paid primarily through a payout on revenues plus participation in employee benefit plans.

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says independent contractor advisors are generally responsible for all their direct costs and receive a higher payout percentage than employee advisors. It describes the options as designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of the firm's support as they need. They may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.

The firm's investor-day deck (published 2025-06-05) lays out the AdvisorChoice spectrum in three groups. Employee: Employee Advisor (RJA) and Advisor Select. Independent contractor: Independent Advisor (ICD) and Banks and Credit Unions. RIA & Custody Services: IAR (Corporate RIA) and RIA & Custody Services. The deck's title says the spectrum "services the largest addressable market in the industry."

Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists headline terms by model. Traditional Employee: minimum 5 years of experience, up to 50% payout, and employee benefits. Advisor Select: minimum 3 years and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue, 70-80% gross payout, and employee benefits. Independent Contractor: 81% to 90% payout. Corporate RIA: minimum 3 years and $50 million in assets under advisement, 81% to 90% payout. Bank & Credit Union: compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James. RIA & Custody Services: the advisor works with the RIA or broker/dealer on compensation, and the RIA is responsible for compliance.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The firm's recruiting pages describe each model's pitch. Traditional Employee (page as of 2026-05-16): book ownership, "no quotas, no product pushing." Advisor Select (page as of 2026-03-11): an employee option giving established advisors the benefits of the employee channel with independence to create their own branch and run its P&L for a higher rate on production. Independent Advisor (page as of 2026-05-19): a "partnership in independence" with a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer, plus a Corporate RIA model for fee-based advisors. RCS (page as of 2026-07-12): strategic, financial and administrative control, "free from retail conflict." Bank & Credit Union (page as of 2026-05-17): 940 advisors across 160 financial institutions, per the page.

claims.text: On the call published 2025-04-23, CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm's "best of both worlds" value proposition (an advisor- and client-focused culture plus leading technology and solutions) resonates with advisors across all affiliation options. On the call published 2026-01-28 he said the firm has the largest addressable market across employee, independent contractor and RIA custody, with critical mass and decades of experience in each, and that this is "not a new venture."

On the call published 2026-07-22, Shoukry said the firm has "all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want" and is "agnostic" and "indifferent" to how an advisor affiliates. He also said advisors differ in how they spend their time: some want to devote close to 100% to clients and planning, which he described as more aligned with the employee option, while others want to run a business, including team, benefits and real estate.

Headcount by channel, per the 2025 10-K (as of September 30). Employees: 3,878 (2025), 3,826 (2024), 3,693 (2023). Independent contractors: 5,065 (2025), 4,961 (2024), 5,019 (2023). Total: 8,943, 8,787 and 8,712.

On the call published 2024-10-23, then-CEO Paul Reilly said RCS had by far the highest percentage growth. In total dollars, he said independents led a couple of years earlier, but that year "the employee channel really led the way." He said the firm no longer sees independents growing faster in up markets and employees in slow markets; it is "really just where we can meet the teams that like an affiliation option." He also expected some improvement in the independent contractor model as cyclical.

RCS client assets, per 10-Q filings, rose across the period. June 30, 2024: $167.2 billion. March 31, 2025: $185.6 billion. June 30, 2025: $201.6 billion. September 30, 2025: $217.3 billion. December 31, 2025: $224.6 billion. March 31, 2026: $228.2 billion. June 30, 2026: $251.3 billion. The firm says RCS growth is partially due to transfers into RCS from its other advisor channels, and it does not expect those transfers to significantly impact results of operations.
For scale, firm-wide Private Client Group assets under administration were $1,574.2 billion at June 30, 2025 and $1,856.5 billion at June 30, 2026.

On the call published 2025-07-23, Shoukry said the firm saw good success across all affiliation options. He said the acceleration rate within the independent channel was "probably higher," while the employee and independent RIA options were also doing very well.

On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said recruiting is broad-based across affiliation options, "maybe more heavily tilted in the last six months on the independent contractor side." He also said revenue mix, including the independent channel's higher payout, pushed the quarter's compensation ratio to 65.4%, slightly above the 65% target.

On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said that over the last year "much more of our recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side," and called it a "mix shift to some extent." He said independent payouts are higher because they cover overhead. He also said the firm is seeing an uptick in employee-channel commits and that employee momentum "continues to tick up."

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says Raymond James's PCG business faces risk from the industry-wide trend of advisors leaving traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or join third-party RIAs (some private-equity backed). It describes this as a highly competitive recruiting environment, and says PCG assets could be hurt if advisors leave or move to an unaffiliated RIA channel. The firm says it mitigates this through succession planning and broad services.

On the call published 2024-10-23, Reilly said a couple of OSJ relationships in the independent contractor division had decided to leave. Roughly $3 billion of AUA left in the fiscal fourth quarter, with about $5 billion more expected early in fiscal 2025. On the call published 2025-01-29, he put the departure of primarily one large branch at about $5 billion of AUA. The 2025 10-K also cites the departure of primarily one large branch in the independent contractor division.

On the call published 2025-01-29, Shoukry said the firm has historically seen about "1% type of regretted attrition." He said the biggest movement of people to RIA had "fortunately" gone to the firm's own RIA, so assets were kept. That is management's statement on moves between models.

Recruiting results into the domestic independent contractor and employee channels, per management. Fiscal 2025, call published 2025-10-22: trailing-12-month production of $407 million (up 21% on the prior record) and approximately $58 billion of client assets at prior firms, with nearly $63 billion across all platforms including RCS. Call published 2026-01-28: nearly $460 million and over $63 billion over the past twelve months, with more than $69 billion including RCS. Call published 2026-04-22: $141 million and nearly $21 billion in the quarter, described as the second highest quarterly result in the firm's history. Call published 2026-07-22: $156 million and nearly $23 billion in the quarter, and $393 million and more than $56 billion over nine months. Management described the sources of recruiting as diverse across affiliation options.

claims.text: On the call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry said recruiting success has been broad-based across the employee, independent contractor and RIA custody channels. On the call published 2026-07-22 he said retention is the foundation of growth and cited a 97% adviser satisfaction rate. He described the pipeline as "broad-based" and "not idiosyncratic," not driven by one firm or one affiliation option.

The firm now breaks out PCG recruiting and retention-related compensation. It was $107 million in the quarter ended December 2025, $111 million in the quarter ended March 2026 and $117 million in the quarter ended June 2026. For the nine months it was $335 million against $274 million a year earlier. On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said the firm prefers recruiting advisors one by one, with 100% of transition assistance going to retention rather than a seller. The firm does not split this expense by affiliation model.

claims.text: On the call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry said the firm is more confident about its competitive positioning than ever. He said that in some ways there is more competition, but competitors increasingly look for an exit in three to five years or compete with "the largest check," while Raymond James emphasizes a long-term, stable, independent platform.

On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry acknowledged "more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups." He said the firm is "absolutely committed to remaining independent." He also said a $1 billion technology investment gives it, in some ways, "less competition than ever," because many similar-culture competitors invest only a fraction of that in technology.

On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said private equity and some strategic firms have been competitive for about five years. He said the firm's focus is to remain the best destination for advisors "across all of our affiliation options," and credited that approach for annualized net new assets of 7% in the first half of the fiscal year.

On the call published 2026-07-22, Shoukry said it is too early to tell how AI affects affiliation options. He said AI will differentiate firms, that smaller firms cannot keep up with the firm's $1.1 billion technology investment, and that AI convergence between affiliation options is "potentially" possible. He also said recruiting "is not something you could turn on and off" and that the firm wants consistency across affiliation options.

The costs that management and the filings tie to the channel mix are as follows. Management cites the higher payout in the independent channel as pushing the compensation ratio up (call published 2026-01-28). The 10-Q (published 2026-05-06) reports a total compensation ratio of 65.8% against 64.8% a year earlier, which it attributes to changes in revenue mix. The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) lists competition from fintechs, banks and other firms as a risk.

adjacent.text: WealthManagement.com (published 2026-10-29) reports that Shoukry said recruiting is spread across all affiliation channels including RIA custody. Per the article, the independent contractor channel sees the most interest in dollar volume, and RCS is growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base. It also reports fiscal-year recruited trailing-12-month production of $538 million, up from $407 million, on more than $82 billion of client assets.

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 call (April 2025), CEO Ted Pick said advisors see an integrated firm offering "compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating", and that the firm is selective about who it takes on.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), management said it would transition all economic hedges for deferred-compensation (DCP) obligations to derivative instruments in the first quarter and "increase the cash component of our advisor compensation". It said this reduces accounting-driven volatility, brings some transitional costs, supports "our overall investment into our financial advisors" and will "help simplify our compensation program".

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) names a risk. Compensation costs to attract and retain employees may increase, and more stringent regulation of employee compensation has shaped the firm's compensation practices, which could adversely affect its ability to hire or retain qualified employees.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: The 1Q26 10-Q (published 2026-05-05) states that deferred compensation for Wealth Management financial advisors is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards. The awards carry vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) states that employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors. The loans are full recourse and due in full on termination of employment. Employee loans totaled $5,039 million in the 2026 column versus $4,858 million in the 2025 column; this covers employee loans generally, not only advisor loans.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program page (page content as of 2026-11-03) lists "Base salary and unlimited earning potential" among what it offers trainee advisors. No payout percentages appear in the evidence.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Merrill: On the 1Q25 call (April 2025), the Bank of America CFO attributed GWIM expense growth of 9% partly to "the cost of hiring to add experienced advisors to the platform in Merrill and the private bank". On the 2Q25 call (July 2025) he again cited the cost of hiring experienced advisors, alongside revenue-related incentives.
claims.source_label: BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2025-03-31 [IR]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2025-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: Its recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) compares AdvisorChoice® affiliation options. Traditional Employee: up to 50% payout plus employee benefits, with a minimum of 5 years of experience. Advisor Select: 70-80% gross payout, with a minimum of 3 years of experience and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue. Independent Contractor: 81% to 90% payout, with a minimum of 3 years of experience and a minimum T12 of $150,000 to join an existing branch or $400,000 to open a new branch.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says employee advisors' compensation primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate, plus participation in employee benefit plans. The firm's one share-based plan covers employees, directors and independent contractor financial advisors (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30).
claims.source_label: RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF 10-Q 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: On the 1Q FY26 call (January 2026) and the 2Q FY26 call (April 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry explained why the firm broke out recruiting and retention costs. He said the firm prefers recruiting advisors one by one rather than acquiring firms because "100% of the transition assistance is going to retention of the adviser" and cultural fit can be ensured. He also said annual recruiting is now comparable to a medium-sized acquisition.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: The Private Client Group supplement (published 2026-07-22) shows recruiting and retention-related compensation of $335 million for the nine months ended June 30, 2026 versus $274 million a year earlier, up 22%. A footnote says it covers cash and equity awards tied to recruiting, retention of existing advisors, or acquisitions, expensed over typically 5 to 10 years.
claims.source_label: RJF supplement 2026-06-30, p.6 [IR]; RJF supplement 2026-06-30, p.18 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: The 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-03-31 says the firm offers loans to prospective financial advisors for recruiting and retention purposes. Offers are contingent on the individual joining or continuing the affiliation, and unfunded commitments were $19 million as of March 31, 2026.

Training - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) describes firm-wide talent development programs. They are "designed to provide employees with the resources to help them achieve their career goals, build management skills and lead their organizations", and the firm states it believes supporting development "contributes to long-term retention". This is not an advisor-specific training program.

Training - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program page (page content as of 2026-11-03) offers "industry leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses". The paths run approximately 13 months for the client-associate and financial-solutions-advisor roles (including three months of licensing for the former). The ADP Financial Advisor stage runs approximately 1-4 years before the trainee becomes a Merrill Core Advisor.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Training - Merrill: On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), the Bank of America CFO said Merrill and the Private Bank continued to add advisors "through our extensive training program and experienced hiring". He said approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.

Training - Merrill: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), the CFO said Merrill is "picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors" but that this "isn't an enormous part of our strategy". He pointed to a training program for people in wealth management as what the firm can "keep driving" to improve net new flows.

Training - Raymond James: On the 3Q FY25 call (July 2025), CEO Shoukry said the firm is investing in "education, training, accreditation, and enhanced capabilities and product solutions" so advisors can serve their most sophisticated private wealth clients.

Training - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says people who want to become advisors can gain branch experience through the Wealth Management Associate Program or move to the Advisor Mastery Program to begin building a client base. It also describes a department providing growth-oriented tools and business coaching, and separate national conferences for employee and independent contractor advisors.
Results - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K reports 9% global voluntary attrition in 2025. This is a firm-wide employee figure, not advisor-specific.

Results - Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), CEO Ted Pick said that when clients trust their financial adviser, "the adviser retention rate is above 99%". This is management's own characterization and no advisor-level data accompanies it in the evidence.

Results - Merrill: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), the Bank of America CFO said the firm "continue[s] to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers" and is driving productivity higher on both newer and existing advisers. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026) he said "adviser attrition is now at near historic lows" and that the aim is to keep growing the sales force. No attrition percentage is given.
claims.source_label: BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-03-31 [IR]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Results - Merrill: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. He said the results reflect strong demand for advice and "our ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform".

Results - Raymond James: On the 4Q FY25 call (October 2025), CEO Shoukry said the firm ended the fiscal year with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year. He credited solid advisor retention and strong recruiting, and cited a robust recruiting pipeline.

Results - Raymond James: On the 2Q FY26 call (April 2026), the CEO said domestic independent contractor and employee recruits had trailing 12-month production of $141 million and nearly $21 billion of client assets at their previous firms. He called this the second highest quarterly result in the firm's history for both measures. On the 3Q FY26 call (July 2026), he cited trailing 12-month production of $156 million and nearly $23 billion of client assets, along with strong retention.

Competitive position and advisor movement - Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 call (April 2025), CEO Pick said people are "coming toward the platform" and that the firm is getting "a lot of inbound inquiry" from advisors. He attributed this to the integrated firm's access to intellectual capital, technology and compensation, and said the firm is selective.

Competitive position and advisor movement - Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CEO tied advisor retention to scale, saying the firm is "the largest distributor in the world of any kind of asset management product" and that reinvestment in its client funnel is how it intends to preserve its moat. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), the CFO said investment is going into product capabilities, referral models and tools such as LeadIQ to match individuals with advisers, with the goal of being clients' principal financial adviser.

Competitive position and advisor movement - Merrill: On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), the Bank of America CFO said both Merrill and the Private Bank "continued to attract talented advisers who are drawn to the breadth of our platform". Merrill's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) pitches the Bank of America brand, lead generation through the global bank and trust division, and its wealth platform.
claims.source_label: BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-06-30 [IR]; MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Competitive position and advisor movement - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) names risks. Advisors are departing traditional firms to independent RIAs, some backed by private equity, creating a "highly competitive recruiting environment". Other firms are offering guaranteed contracts, upfront payments and increased compensation. Reported AUA may be negatively affected if the firm fails to retain or recruit advisors.

Competitive position and advisor movement - Raymond James: On the 1Q FY26 call (January 2026), CEO Shoukry said recruiting is broad-based across affiliation options, though more heavily tilted toward independent contractors in the prior six months. He said advisors come from wirehouses, regionals and other independents, and acknowledged "more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups".

Areas of pullback or losses - Raymond James: On the 4Q FY24 call (October 2024), then-CEO Paul Reilly said a couple of OSJ relationships in the independent contractor division decided to leave the platform. About $3 billion of AUA left in the fiscal fourth quarter, and approximately $5 billion more was expected to transfer in early fiscal 2025.

questions.text: Compare how Schwab and Raymond James describe their value proposition to independent advisors.

parts.text: How Schwab describes its value proposition to independent advisors (Schwab Advisor Services custody, technology, service, and support).
parts.keyword_query: Advisor Services independent registered investment advisors RIAs value proposition custody platform technology service support scale clients independence open architecture

parts.text: How Raymond James describes its value proposition to independent advisors (Independent Contractors channel and RJ Financial Services, and Raymond James Investment Advisors Services).
parts.keyword_query: independent contractor affiliation advisors Raymond James Financial Services RJ Employee Institution Custody Services value proposition technology support platform flexibility recruiting independent advisors

parts.text: How Schwab describes its value proposition to independent advisors (Schwab Advisor Services custody, technology, service, and support).
parts.keyword_query: Advisor Services independent registered investment advisors RIAs value proposition custody platform technology service support scale clients independence open architecture

parts.text: How Raymond James describes its value proposition to independent advisors (Independent Contractors channel and RJ Financial Services, and Raymond James Investment Advisors Services).
parts.keyword_query: independent contractor affiliation advisors Raymond James Financial Services RJ Employee Institution Custody Services value proposition technology support platform flexibility recruiting independent advisors

claims.text: Value proposition - Schwab: On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CEO Rick Wurster said that in Advisor Services Schwab is "deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone." He cited lending support, alternatives capability, an institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform with funds from nearly 60 managers, and the launch of Advisor ProDirect to help breakaway advisors on their path to independence.

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Wurster said "we're winning across every dimension" in Advisor Services. He said it is hard for other firms to compete with Schwab's "size, scale, and the breadth and strength of our capabilities." He pointed to the custody offering, consulting and expertise, support for the drive to independence, and product capabilities and platform. He credited roughly 6.5% organic growth last year to these.

Value proposition - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says Schwab, through Advisor Services, is one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking and support services to RIAs. Management believes it maintains its competitive position primarily through sales, support, technology and business consulting teams "dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed." It says it focuses on superior service and uses technology to give RIAs a "highly-developed, scalable platform."

Value proposition - Schwab (technology): The 2025 10-K describes the Advisor Services website as the core platform for RIAs, covering account opening, money movement, transfer of assets, trading and communication with the service team. It also lists integrations with third-party CRM, portfolio management, trade order management and planning platforms. It names Schwab Advisor Portfolio Connect (free to advisors to manage Schwab accounts), thinkpipes trading and iRebal rebalancing.

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster said "we continue to have the leading custodial offer." He described a newly launched structured asset lending program that lets advisors' clients borrow against alternative investments and restricted or private shares, so advisors keep the wealth relationship instead of introducing a big bank. He said "our value proposition to advisers has never been stronger." He also said Schwab is enhancing digital RIA workflows (move money, account open, account maintenance) so routine work gets done faster and with fewer errors.

Value proposition - Schwab: In its Investor Day deck (published 2026-05-14), Schwab describes "the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service."

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said Schwab built its adviser business "around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed." He said it serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets, on a platform combining custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support. He said more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as custodian last year, "more than 3x the number of the next closest provider." He also said Schwab is #1 by RIA custodial assets.

Value proposition - Schwab (AI): The 3Q26 earnings release (October 2026) says Schwab partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors directly to the independent RIAs it serves. In the release, the CEO describes Schwab's "leading value proposition" as continuing to resonate with investors and RIAs.

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the fiscal 1Q25 call (April 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry described a "best of both worlds" value proposition, with an advisor- and client-focused culture plus capabilities, technologies and solutions. He said the firm's strong balance sheet is increasingly important to prospective advisors. He said pipelines are strong across "our affiliation options."

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the calls of July 2025 and October 2025, Shoukry repeated the "best of both worlds" value proposition, saying it resonates across all affiliation options. He added that the firm's "strong balance sheet and commitment to independence" is a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives. He described investments in private wealth education, training, accreditation and product solutions for advisors' most sophisticated clients.

Value proposition - Raymond James: The Investor Day deck (published 2025-06-05) says its AdvisorChoice spectrum "services the largest addressable market in the industry." The spectrum runs from employee through independent contractor (independent advisor, banks and credit unions, corporate RIA) to RIA & Custody Services. The deck adds that the movement to "independence" is not channel-specific.

Value proposition - Raymond James: The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says its AdvisorChoice® affiliation options include independent contractors and employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services division. It says independent contractor advisors are responsible for their direct costs and so receive a higher payout percentage than employee advisors. It says these options are "designed to help our advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of our support as they determine they need."

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the fiscal 4Q25 call (January 2026), Shoukry said the firm offers "a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture, coupled with leading technology and solutions." He said this, with its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, is a differentiator. He cited the private wealth advisor program, an expanded alternative investments platform and a newly launched proprietary AI operations agent named Rai. He also said Raymond James has the largest addressable market across employee, independent contractor and RIA custody options, with critical mass and decades of experience in each.

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said "advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities." He said the firm pairs a client-focused culture with leading technologies, products and solutions. He said this, combined with its balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence, sets it apart. He cited a technology spend of more than $1.1 billion annually.

Value proposition - Raymond James (independent contractor page): The firm's recruiting page for independent advisors (page content as of 2026-05-19) is titled "A partnership in independence." It says independent contractors can access the firm's full capabilities "at a level that's right for your business," backed by a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer. It lists private wealth concierge support, technology "shaped by advisors," marketing, succession and acquisition guidance, business consulting, paraplanning, admin extension and local divisional support.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-05-19 [IR]

claims.text: Value proposition - Raymond James (RIA & Custody Services): The firm's RCS page (page content as of 2026-07-12) offers RIAs "true strategic, financial and administrative control" "free from retail conflict," using as much or as little of the firm's support as they need. It lists a dedicated service associate, a self-clearing NYSE firm, an integrated technology platform that can incorporate third-party applications, transitions management, practice management, marketing, recruiting assistance, succession planning and acquisition support, and wealth strategies for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-07-12 [IR]

claims.text: Value proposition - Raymond James (advisor feedback): The firm's Investor Day deck (published 2025-06-05) cites its 2025 Voice of the Advisor survey, showing 90% advisor satisfaction with technology, service center and support. On the July 2026 call, Shoukry pointed to "near record levels of adviser satisfaction" and to the combination of balance sheet, long-term focus and commitment to independence. He said the firm will keep investing in private wealth tools, automation, process improvement and AI within its more than $1.1 billion annual technology spend.

Risk named by Raymond James: The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says that although independent RIAs and broker-dealers it provides custody, clearing and back-office support to are exclusively responsible for their operations, supervision and compliance, the firm "has been, and may in the future be, named as defendants in litigation involving their clients."

claims.text: Explicit statements - Merrill: Bank of America's investor-day deck (published 2025-11-05, GWIM segment) sets out a "Wealth Continuum" that labels a "Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)" tier alongside "High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM)". It is the only text in the evidence provided that names a mass-affluent tier for any of the five firms. The label comes from the GWIM deck, so it is Bank of America's wording, not a standalone Merrill disclosure.

Explicit statements - Merrill: The same deck lists, as a foundational belief, that "the Wealth Continuum allows us to deliver as one company and is our engine for lasting growth" and that "we have the capabilities to deliver for every client in the way they want to be served". This is the firm's own framing and is not specific to the mass-affluent tier.

Explicit statements - Schwab: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44 prefer to consolidate wealth and banking relationships. He said households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one financial services firm "jumped 11 percentage points year-over-year to 22%". He speaks of "affluent" clients, not "mass affluent".

Explicit statements - Schwab: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said the retail business is "built to win across generations, wealth tiers, investing styles and engagement preferences". He added that roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high net worth and high net worth households.
Definition and thresholds - Merrill: Bank of America's investor-day deck (2025-11-05, GWIM) gives the mass-affluent tier as $500K - $1MM and the high-net-worth tier as $1MM - $10MM.

Definition and thresholds - Merrill: The 2025 Bank of America 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business is "a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets". Bank of America Private Bank, with Merrill's Private Wealth Management, targets high net worth and ultra high net worth clients.

Strategy, advice models and products - Merrill: The 2025 Bank of America 10-K describes a "high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors" for clients with over $250,000 in investable assets. It says Merrill provides "tailored solutions" through "a full set of investment management, brokerage, banking and retirement products". The filing does not tie this to the mass-affluent tier.

Strategy, advice models and products - Merrill: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the Bank of America CFO said that advisor productivity, disciplined pricing, digital engagement and AI tools "continue to expand our capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale". He said 67% of Merrill clients now have banking relationships with the firm.

Growth priorities, competition and results - Merrill: Bank of America reported ~3.3K net new $500K+ households added at Merrill Wealth Management in 1Q26 (press release, 2026-04-15) and ~5.4K in 2Q26 (press release, 2026-07-14). On the 3Q26 call (October 2026) the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%, and said "these results reflect strong demand for advice". The $500K+ count is a wider group than the $500K-$1MM tier the deck labels mass affluent.

Definition - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (period ended 2025-09-30, published 2025-11-25) says financial advisors primarily affiliate directly, either as employees or as independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division. The 10-K calls its independent contractor financial advisors "independent advisors". It says financial advisors associated with RCS firms "are not included in our financial advisor counts".

Includes - Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) reports a total of 20,514 financial advisors at period end. It also splits the count between the U.S. (19,647) and Canada (867).
