claims.text: Cerulli's Great Wealth Transfer report (published 2025-10-29) projects that households will transfer $123.7 trillion to heirs ($105 trillion) and charities ($18 trillion) between now and 2048. It expects Generation Xers to inherit $39 trillion and Millennials $46 trillion. Women in the Baby Boomer and older generations are expected to receive $40 trillion in 'horizontal' transfers as they outlive their husbands. Women in younger generations are expected to receive $47 trillion of the wealth transferred intergenerationally.

Cerulli (2025-10-29) says trillions of dollars are already changing hands annually and the transfer is 'in full swing'. It says women and next-generation clients differ in service preferences from current client demographics. Cerulli expects those differences to shift market share to the firms best prepared to meet these recipients' needs.

The UBS next-generation report (published 2026-04-22) estimates that USD 83 trillion in private wealth will change hands globally over the next two to three decades. UBS attributes this to aging demographics, longer life expectancies and decades of rising asset prices. The UBS and Cerulli figures are stated on different bases and time horizons as printed, so they are not directly comparable.

Edward Jones's 2Q25 10-Q (published 2025-08-08) says net new assets decreased 10% versus 2Q24. It attributes the higher asset outflows partly to 'an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm'. The 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) repeats these factors for the first nine months of 2025, when net new assets decreased 4%.

Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states that its ability to compete and adapt its business model may be adversely impacted by the evolving financial services industry and generational wealth transfer. It cites changing client demographics, preferences and values.

Schwab's 3Q26 deck (published 2026-10-15) shows 80% of retail assets held by ultra-high and high net worth households and ~75% of assets retained in a wealth transfer event. On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-15), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab is 'well positioned to continue serving future generations when that wealth is passed on'. He also said its retention rate around wealth transfers is 'extremely high'.

Schwab's 2Q25 call (2025-07-18): CEO Rick Wurster said one in six new-to-firm retail households were under the age of 24. He said more than 30% were under 30 and nearly 60% under 40. On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-21) he said Gen Z investors were nearly a third of new retail client accounts opened in 2025. On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-15) he said approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials.

claims.text: Schwab's 3Q25 call (2025-10-16): in discussing crypto, Wurster said it 'will certainly appeal to young investors', but 'we are absolutely crushing it with young investors today'.

Schwab's 3Q26 call (2026-10-15): Wurster said retail clients with a dedicated financial consultant generate approximately 3x the household NNA, 5x the managed investing net flows of comparable unassigned households and 3x the transfer of assets ratio. He said Schwab is investing in people and technology to build and retain relationships 'for the decades to come'. The 3Q26 deck frames Schwab's retail offering as serving generations from 'next-gen to retirees'.

Schwab's 1Q26 deck (published 2026-04-16) lists a 'Schwab Teen Investor Account' among its products and solutions. Its investor-day deck (published 2026-05-14) lists the Schwab Starter Kit and the Schwab Teen Investor Account for younger investors. The same deck lists consultant relationships, dedicated service and relationship pricing for high and ultra-high net worth clients.

claims.text: Raymond James's investor-day recruiting deck (published 2025-06-05) lists a 'Next gen advisor strategy' alongside collaborative recruiting across channels and a West Coast and Northeast focus. The excerpt gives no detail on the strategy.

On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-28), Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm is continuing platform investments to retain and attract advisors. He cited its private wealth advisor program and expanded alternative investments platform, which support advisors who focus on high-net-worth clients.

InvestmentNews (trade press, published 2026-09-29) reports that Raymond James's high-net-worth effort includes estate and charitable planning capabilities and 'intergenerational wealth strategies' as tools advisors can use. It says the Raymond James Private Wealth Advisor designation program, launched in September 2022, serves advisors who specialize in households with generally at least $5 million in investable assets. As of September 2026, nearly 450 advisors have earned the designation, according to Raymond James. The trade source calls the program a recruitment and retention signal. This is trade-press reporting, not a firm statement on heirs.

Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says the Partnership addresses its strategic risks through initiatives. The risks it names are competition for clients and personnel amid the evolving industry and generational wealth transfer, changing client demographics, technology, AI and regulatory changes. claims.text: Definition - Schwab: the 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) defines 'Net new client assets' as 'total inflows of client cash and securities to Schwab less client outflows. Inflows include dividends and interest; outflows include commissions and fees. Capital gains distributions are excluded.' It defines 'core net new client assets' as net new client assets before significant one-time inflows or outflows, such as acquisitions/divestitures or extraordinary flows (generally greater than $25 billion ($10 billion prior to 2025)) relating to a specific client, and activity from off-platform brokered CDs issued by CSB, noting these flows may span multiple reporting periods. Definition - Edward Jones: the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says net new assets 'represents cash and securities inflows and outflows, excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions received by U.S. clients.' Definition - Raymond James: its 3Q26 press release (published 2026-07-22) says domestic Private Client Group net new assets 'represents domestic Private Client Group client inflows, including dividends and interest, less domestic Private Client Group client outflows, including commissions, advisory fees, and other fees.' The annualized growth percentage is based on the beginning domestic Private Client Group assets under administration balance for the period. The metric is for the domestic Private Client Group, not the whole firm.

claims.text: Total client assets - Morgan Stanley: The 3Q26 Wealth Management supplement (published 2026-10-14) reports Wealth Management total client assets of $8,433 billion at Sep 30, 2026. Within that, advisor-led client assets were $6,631 billion and self-directed client assets were $1,802 billion. Stock plan unvested public assets of $638 billion are listed separately under the workplace channel.
claims.source_label: MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30, p.8 [IR]

claims.text: Total client assets - Schwab: On the 3Q26 call (published 2026-10-15), the CEO said Schwab's adviser business serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets. These are independent advisers' firms on Schwab's custody platform. The evidence gives no Schwab wealth-advisor or employee-advisor channel total.

Total client assets - Edward Jones: The Q2 2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) says the Partnership ended the second quarter of 2026 with $2.6 trillion of assets under care ("AUC"), including $1.2 trillion of advisory programs AUC.

Total client assets - Merrill: The 3Q26 Bank of America supplement (published 2026-10-14) reports client balances for Merrill Wealth Management of $4,240,601 million at Sep 30, 2026. Bank of America calls this measure "client balances", not "client assets".

Total client assets - Raymond James: The fiscal Q3 2026 press release (published 2026-07-22) reports client assets under administration of $1,922.4 billion at June 30, 2026. Private Client Group assets under administration were $1,856.5 billion, and Private Client Group assets in fee-based accounts were $1,153.8 billion.
claims.source_label: RJF press - Private Client Group segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Advisor count - Edward Jones: The Q2 2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) says the Partnership ended the second quarter with 20,514 financial advisors, against 20,309 a year earlier. The 10-Q's segment table also lists period-end advisor counts of 19,647 and 867 for the current period, and 19,435 and 874 a year earlier. The 10-Q says the Partnership has two operating segments, U.S. and Canada.

Advisor count - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) states that Raymond James had 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors affiliated with it as of September 30, 2025. The same passage gives Private Client Group client assets under administration of $1.67 trillion at that date. The firm-wide count is a combined employee and independent-contractor figure. The 10-K does not give a split between the two in the text provided.

Definitions and comparability - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) says Wealth Management client assets cover advisor-led brokerage, investment advisory, custody and related services. They also cover self-directed brokerage and investment advisory services, financial and wealth planning, and workplace services including stock plan administration and retirement plan services. The 3Q26 supplement (published 2026-10-14) defines advisor-led client assets as assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned. It defines self-directed client assets as active accounts that are not advisor-led, with active meaning at least $25 in assets. The 3Q26 supplement also splits out stock plan unvested public assets under the workplace channel. The Q2 2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) says stock plan unvested assets are not included in client assets.
claims.source_label: MS 10-K - Wealth Management segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; MS supplement 2026-09-30, p.15 [IR]; MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30, p.8 [IR]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Definitions and comparability - Schwab: The 3Q26 press release (published 2026-10-15) describes client assets of $13.33 trillion alongside 40.3 million active brokerage accounts, 5.9 million workplace plan participant accounts and 2.4 million banking accounts. The release also describes custodial, operational and trading support for independent, fee-based investment advisors. The May 2026 investor-day deck (published 2026-05-14) states that Schwab Advisor Network advisors are independent and are not employees or agents of Charles Schwab & Co. Schwab's client assets therefore mix self-directed, workplace and independent-advisor custody assets.

Definitions and comparability - Edward Jones: The Q1 2026 10-Q (published 2026-05-07) describes the Partnership as operating in the U.S. and Canada, with more than 20,000 financial advisors serving more than 9 million clients and $2.4 trillion in client assets under care as of March 27, 2026. Assets and advisor counts are reported at the Partnership level, covering both countries.

Definitions and comparability - Merrill: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business as a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets. It says Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill's Private Wealth Management business, serves high net worth and ultra high net worth clients. Merrill's client balances are reported as a line within the GWIM segment.
claims.source_label: BAC 10-K - GWIM segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; BAC supplement - GWIM segment 2026-09-30, p.18 [IR]

claims.text: Definitions and comparability - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says Financial advisors can be employees, independent contractors, or employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division. Independent contractor advisors are generally responsible for their own direct costs and receive a higher payout percentage than employee advisors. The 10-K states that advisors associated with RCS firms are not included in Raymond James's financial advisor counts, although their client assets are included in AUA. RCS AUA totaled $217.3 billion at September 30, 2025. Raymond James's assets-under-administration totals therefore include assets whose advisors are not in the count.

claims.text: Payout structure - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) attributes higher Wealth Management compensation primarily to an increase in the "formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenue." The 10-K does not give the formula's rates.

Payout structure - Morgan Stanley: The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) again cites an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors, based on higher revenues, as a driver of compensation and benefits expense.

Payout structure - Morgan Stanley: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-11-04) says the fee a client pays is a factor in calculating Financial Advisor compensation. If the fee rate is below a certain threshold, the firm gives the advisor credit for less than the total fee. The brochure says this gives advisors a financial incentive not to reduce fees below that threshold. It does not state the threshold.

Payout structure - Merrill: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-10-30) refers to an "incentive compensation grid." An Advisor is subject to a reduction in that grid if they fail to achieve growth for two consecutive years in the assets and liabilities component of the incentive award. Merrill states that it considers and approves its compensation program from year to year and that the criteria can change.

Payout structure - Merrill: The brochure (published 2026-10-30) says an Advisor may negotiate a higher Merrill Lynch Fee Rate when recommending Style Manager strategies with no or lower manager fees. Merrill discloses that it retains a certain percentage of the Merrill Lynch Fee, and that the arrangement gives the Advisor a financial incentive.
claims.source_label: MER adv 2026-10-30, p.32 [filing]; MER adv 2026-10-30, p.33 [filing]

claims.text: Payout structure - Schwab: Schwab's advisory brochure (published 2026-10-15) says financial consultants (FCs) receive compensation for enrolling clients in the Schwab Wealth Advisory (SWA) Program and for providing ongoing service. It says that compensation may vary with the type of program or services a client chooses. As a result, FCs may earn more on SWA assets than on commission-based brokerage accounts or certain other advisory programs. The brochure points to schwab.com/representative-compensation for more detail.

Payout structure - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says financial advisor compensation and benefits expense increased 12% to $6,969 in 2025. It attributes the increase primarily to increases in revenues on which commissions are earned.

Payout structure - Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) says financial advisor compensation and benefits expense increased 18% and 16% in the second quarter and first half of 2026, to $2,001 and $3,876. It again attributes the increase to increases in revenues on which commissions are earned.

Payout structure - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) describes two models. Employee financial advisors' compensation "primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate," and they also participate in the firm's employee benefit plans. Independent contractor advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee advisors.

Payout structure - Raymond James: Its affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists headline payouts. Traditional Employee: up to 50% payout. Advisor Select: 70-80% gross payout. Independent Contractor: 81% to 90% payout. Corporate RIA: 81% to 90% payout. For Bank & Credit Union, the page describes a compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James. For RIA & Custody Services, the RIA or broker/dealer determines compensation.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Payout structure - Raymond James: On the fiscal 2Q26 call (published 2026-04-22), CEO Paul Shoukry said independent payouts are higher than employee payouts because independent advisors cover their overhead, real estate and health insurance. He added that "even on the employee side, we have tiered payout systems," so advisors move up the payout grid as production increases.

Payout structure - Raymond James: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-09-14) says that, depending on annual revenue generation with the firm, an advisor can receive a higher portion of the fee paid to the firm. The firm says this may incentivize the advisor to increase revenue generation to obtain higher payout percentages. The client's fee stays the same. Advisors may also share portions of their payout with other advisors.

Salary, bonus and profit sharing - Morgan Stanley: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-11-04) says a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor (MSVA) is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus. An MSVA does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee. The evidence does not give a salary or bonus structure for traditional Financial Advisors.

Salary, bonus and profit sharing - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program web page (page content as of 2026-11-03) lists "Base salary and unlimited earning potential" as a program feature. The program is for new advisors, with the aim that they progress to Merrill Core Advisor.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Salary, bonus and profit sharing - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes a compensation package for Schwab employees generally. It includes base pay, performance-based incentive pay, equity awards and recognition awards. The description is not specific to financial consultants.

Salary, bonus and profit sharing - Schwab: In its 3Q26 deck (published 2026-10-15), Schwab says it uses adjusted diluted EPS and return on tangible common equity as components of performance criteria for employee bonus and certain executive management incentive compensation arrangements. The Compensation Committee of CSC's Board maintains discretion in evaluating performance against these criteria.

Salary, bonus and profit sharing - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says a significant portion of the Partnership's profits is allocated to variable compensation and paid to associates as bonuses and profit sharing. It calls this a key component of the firm's performance-based compensation model. Variable compensation increased 11% to $2,710 in 2025. Note 15 says financial advisor bonuses are determined by the overall Partnership's profitability as well as the performance of individual financial advisors.

Salary, bonus and profit sharing - Edward Jones: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-03-27) says the Program Fee, assets under care and Reserve Line Advance balances impact most financial advisors' eligibility for a bonus and the bonus amount. They may also affect eligibility for certain limited partnership profits interest in The Jones Financial Companies, L.L.L.P. (the "Profits Interest"). The brochure calls this a conflict of interest. It also says advisors may receive compensation on Reserve Line Advances depending on branch profitability.

Salary, bonus and profit sharing - Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) says variable compensation increased 33% and 27% in the second quarter and first half of 2026, to $780 and $1,528. It attributes the increase to increased branch profitability and overall Firm profitability.

Salary, bonus and profit sharing - Raymond James: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-09-14) says newly affiliated RJA financial advisors in the Advisor Mastery Program may receive a salary in addition to advisory fees, or in addition to commissions and trails in brokerage accounts, for a period of time.

Deferred, retention and recruiting awards - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) says compensation and benefits expenses include amortization of deferred cash and equity awards and changes in the fair value of the referenced notional DCP investments.

Deferred, retention and recruiting awards - Morgan Stanley: A press release (published 2026-10-14) defines "DCP" as certain employee deferred cash-based compensation programs. It says hedges for Wealth Management DCP awards were primarily transitioned to derivative instruments beginning in 1Q26, with the hedge result recorded in compensation expense in the same period the DCP award vests. As a result, the firm no longer presents non-GAAP measures excluding DCP.
claims.source_label: MS press - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30 [filing]; MS supplement 2026-09-30, p.16 [IR]

claims.text: Deferred, retention and recruiting awards - Merrill: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-10-30) says Advisors are eligible for a compensation award, payable over a defined period of time, from an incentive program. The program is currently based on meeting growth targets from the prior year in new households and in assets and liabilities. The brochure also lists drivers of the assets-and-liabilities component, including movement of client assets into advisory program accounts and clients' use of banking and lending services. It says Advisors do not receive additional compensation as a result of advisory client assets held in the Cash Sweep Program.

Deferred, retention and recruiting awards - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) lists equity awards and recognition awards among the components of the employee compensation package, in addition to base pay and performance-based incentive pay. It does not separately describe advisor retention or recruiting awards.

Deferred, retention and recruiting awards - Edward Jones: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-03-27) says most financial advisors are eligible for the Edward Jones Travel Award Program, which includes domestic and international travel or a cash award in lieu of a trip. Eligibility is based on the amount of new and existing assets under care of a financial advisor, which the brochure says creates an additional conflict of interest.

Deferred, retention and recruiting awards - Raymond James: On the fiscal 4Q25 call (published 2025-10-22), the CFO said adjusted compensation expense in fiscal 2025 included amortization of transition assistance provided to recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors. The aggregate amount was $355 million, an increase of approximately 11% compared to fiscal 2024.

Deferred, retention and recruiting awards - Raymond James: Footnotes to the fiscal 3Q26 supplement (published 2026-07-22) say PCG recruiting and retention-related compensation covers cash and equity awards issued for recruiting, as retention for existing advisors, or in conjunction with acquisitions. The awards are expensed over the requisite service period, typically between 5 and 10 years. The segment table shows this line at 117 ($ in millions) for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and 335 for the nine months ended June 30, 2026, up 22%.
claims.source_label: RJF supplement 2026-06-30, p.18 [IR]; RJF supplement 2026-06-30, p.6 [IR]

claims.text: Referral pay - Raymond James: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-09-14) says the Institutional Account Participation Program (IAPP) pays referral fees to financial advisors who refer institutional clients to Raymond James Investment Management or its subsidiary advisers, as a percentage of the management fee earned. Advisors and the firm may also refer clients to Canadian affiliates and receive a referral fee for accounts opened.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley's 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) reports firm-wide compensation and benefits expenses of $29,216 million in 2025, up 12%. It attributes the increase primarily to the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors and higher discretionary incentive compensation within Institutional Securities, both on higher revenues, and to higher salary expenses.

claims.text: WealthManagement.com (trade press, 2026-11-12) reports Raymond James will add $18.7 billion and 70 advisors to its Financial Institutions Division as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp. Advisors are expected to transition in May 2027. FID president Stephen Kruchten called it "a significant and highly strategic expansion" of the relationship with Pinnacle Financial Partners.

A trade-press item (2026-11-12) says the firm "recently posted record quarterly client assets and strong recruiting gains across its advisor channels," with CEO Paul Shoukry crediting flexibility in affiliation options. It also says Raymond James recruited a Southwest Florida team managing about $700 million to FID in October.

InvestmentNews (trade press, 2026-11-06) reports Raymond James & Associates added a Washington, D.C. team, KKM Wealth Partners within Alex. Brown. The team came from PNC Private Bank, where it managed over $1.5 billion. The article adds that RJA announced a $700 million team earlier that week, the second in as many weeks at that size.

InvestmentNews (2026-11-06) reports Ricardo Baptiste rejoined Ameriprise after a six-year stint at Raymond James. He brings $193 million in client assets. This is a reported departure from Raymond James.

InvestmentNews (2026-11-05) reports Samuel Mintz and Stephen Gow moved from Truist Investment Services to Raymond James & Associates in Richmond, Virginia, as the Mintz & Gow Group, adding more than $1.2 billion in client assets. The article says Raymond James ended its fiscal year with a record 8,943 advisors, up 2% year-over-year.

WealthManagement.com (2026-11-05) reports Raymond James's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings showed $538 million in trailing 12-month production from recruited advisors entering its domestic independent contractor and employee channels, up from $407 million the prior year. Those advisors represented more than $82 billion in client assets. Shoukry said recruiting success spans all affiliation channels, including RIA custody, and independent contractor draws the most interest by dollar volume.

InvestmentNews (2026-11-04) reports a four-advisor team from UBS Financial Services, 42° North Advisors, joined RJA in Beachwood, Ohio, with more than $700 million in client assets. The article calls it part of a "consistent run" of RJA recruiting from UBS through 2026.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29), covering the fiscal fourth-quarter call, reports record quarter-end client assets under administration of $1.87 trillion, up 1% sequentially and 12% year-over-year. Private Client Group had record net revenue of $3.06 billion, up 15% year-over-year, and pre-tax income of $458 million, up 10%. Domestic PCG net new assets rose 88% for the fiscal year to a record of more than $98 billion, and quarterly net new assets were nearly $23 billion. Non-GAAP EPS was $3.59 on revenue of $4.74 billion, up 13% (EPS figure per Seeking Alpha, as cited by the outlet).

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) reports the firm no longer reports advisor headcount. It had about 8,900 advisors when headcount was last broken out. This differs from the 2026-11-05 InvestmentNews statement of a record 8,943 advisors.
claims.source_label: RJF trade 2026-10-29 [trade press (indicative only)]; RJF trade 2026-11-05 [trade press (indicative only)]

claims.text: On M&A, WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) quotes Shoukry saying the firm looks for wealth-management acquisitions that are a good cultural and strategic fit. He said "We don't do acquisitions to slash costs," and that deals must make financial sense for Raymond James and the sellers.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) quotes Shoukry saying Raymond James has "the largest total addressable market based on having all of the affiliation options at scale." He said the RIA custody division is growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-23) reports Raymond James recruited a Southwest Florida team managing about $700 million to its Financial Institutions Division. The team joined Pinnacle Financial Partners' investment program from Truist Investment Services.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-16) reports the Edward Fitzpatrick Group, with Raymond James for about 23 years and $3.3 billion in client assets, left to open a Janney Montgomery Scott office in Houston. Advisor Lance Murphy, who oversaw more than $200 million, is also leaving Raymond James to join the team. This is a reported departure.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-08) reports four practices with more than $1 billion in client assets left Raymond James Financial Services for Ascentis Independent Advisors. They will continue to use Raymond James as primary custodian.

InvestmentNews and WealthManagement.com (2026-09-29) report Raymond James launched Private Wealth Guided Portfolios. These risk-based models combine equity and fixed income with a dedicated alternatives sleeve covering private markets and hedged strategies. PCG President Tash Elwyn said the firm is "committed to being a destination for private wealth advisors." Nearly 450 advisors have earned the Raymond James Private Wealth Advisor designation since 2022.

InvestmentNews (2026-09-29) says the models are built by Raymond James's Asset Management Services division with the Private Markets and Alternatives team. The same article says the firm's Clark Capital Management Group acquisition, announced in January 2026 (more than $46 billion under management), closed in May 2026 as an independent boutique within Raymond James Investment Management. These are background items, not new in the window.

InvestmentNews (2026-09-29) says the firm is piloting an AI-powered advisor assistant called Raimond. It also says Shoukry emphasizes building advisor ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions.

WealthManagement.com and InvestmentNews (2026-09-24) report Raymond James added a $1.25 billion Iowa team (Greenwood Wealth Partners, from D.M. Kelly & Company) to its employee channel. It also added a roughly $500 million five-advisor team (Harris Wealth Partners, Rochester, N.Y., from Commonwealth Financial Network) to its independent channel.

WealthManagement.com (2026-09-16) reports Raymond James launched a firm-wide SIMPLE IRA Employer Advisory and Consulting Services Program, per an SEC filing, made available to its roughly 8,900 advisors. It is partnered with Capital Group American Funds.
InvestmentNews (2026-09-02) reports a team that previously managed more than $550 million at UBS joined RJA in The Woodlands, Texas.

InvestmentNews (2026-08-26) reports Jeffrey Stillwell joined Raymond James Financial Services in New Jersey from Ameriprise Financial Services with about $240 million. He cited investment banking access and lending solutions for business-owner clients.
InvestmentNews (2026-08-21) reports Adam Pearsall joined RJA in Glens Falls, New York, from UBS with more than $400 million in client assets.
InvestmentNews (2026-08-19) reports Roberto De Jesus joined Raymond James Financial Services from Edward Jones after 18 years there, bringing about $199 million in client assets.

On outlook, InvestmentNews (2026-11-05) says the firm "has signaled it expects continued momentum, with healthy pipelines of advisor commitments heading into the coming year." This is trade-press characterization, not a direct management quote.

A source said the team produced $3.1 million in annual revenue. The article says Marsden took over the Northeast region in June 2023.

Jones & Co. in Texas.

AdvisorHub (2026-11-16) reports that Merrill executives said in October that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year. It says the firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 and returned to it after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. This is trade-press characterization of a strategic shift, not a 2026 leadership change.

Morgan Advisors team. It also reports that J.P. Morgan Wealth hired another Merrill alum, Linda Patel, as Southeast Regional Director. InvestmentNews (2026-10-14) reports that Nick Economos launched Economos Private Wealth through LPL, bringing approximately $580 million in assets from Merrill Lynch.

claims.text: InvestmentNews (trade press, 2026-10-16) reports that Wells Fargo and Merrill agreed to a combined $4.4 million settlement with state securities regulators over unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions. Merrill Lynch faces restitution on approximately $549,000 in excess commissions from September 30, 2020 through October 1, 2025. The firms must also pay administrative fines and investigation costs. WealthManagement.com (2026-10-15) reports the same matter.
claims.source_label: MER trade 2026-10-16 [trade press (indicative only)]; MER trade 2026-10-15 [trade press (indicative only)]

claims.text: On the 3Q26 earnings materials (published 2026-10-14), Bank of America's supplement shows Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $5,905 million in 3Q26, against $5,579 million in 1Q26, $5,711 million in 2Q26 and $5,261 million in 3Q25 (dollars in millions). Merrill Wealth Management client balances were $4,240,601 million at the end of 3Q26, against $3,815,389 million at 1Q26 and $3,896,124 million at 3Q25.

The 3Q26 earnings release (2026-10-14) lists Merrill Wealth Management highlights: $4.2 trillion in client balances, $1.9 trillion in AUM balances, ~4.2K net new $500K+ households added in 3Q26, 70K digital appointments scheduled in the quarter, and 87% of Merrill households digitally active. CFO Alastair Borthwick said on the call that Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. He also said 67% of Merrill clients have banking relationships with the firm.
claims.source_label: BAC press - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [filing]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [IR]

claims.text: InvestmentNews (trade press, 2026-10-14) quotes Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management, saying client sales of alternative investments at Merrill Lynch increased 19% in the quarter. The article says that while he did not mention new AI tools, the message was clear that the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities. That is the reporter's reading, not a Merrill statement.

Business leadership recognitions listed in the 3Q26 earnings release (2026-10-14) include >300 Merrill advisors on Barron's 2026 Top 1,500 Financial Advisors, 19 Merrill advisors on Barron's 2026 Top 100 Women Financial Advisors, and 24 Merrill advisors on Financial Planning's 2026 Top 40 Brokers Under 40. The release also lists 'Merrill Recognized by WealthManagement.com for Practice Management.' These are firm-selected third-party recognitions.

InvestmentNews (trade press, 2026-10-02) reports that Merrill Lynch agreed to pay $39 million to settle a class action alleging it paid close-to-zero interest on cash in retirement accounts. The preliminary settlement covers Merrill Edge account holders between December 15, 2016 and March 15, 2020, and Merrill denied wrongdoing. The article says this is on top of a $25 million SEC penalty in January 2025, for a combined $64 million. The settlement requires court approval.

RIABiz (trade press, 2026-09-29) reports that Merrill has created new fees for third-party asset managers, effective Jan. 1, 2027, disclosed in Form ADV updates. The data analytics fees run between $125,000 and $860,000 per firm per year for actively managed products. The article says a 'support fee' revenue share runs from 0.02% to a maximum 0.1%, up to $1 million per $1 billion managed. Merrill's filing states it will have a financial incentive to recommend products from firms that pay for data analytics over those that do not.

A Merrill press release (2026-09-15) announced two new services, Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), available through the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program. Managed Account Advisors LLC implements them. The release says both are optional, with no additional IAP Program Fees charged.
The same 2026-09-15 Merrill release states that no additional IAP Program Fees are charged for the new TET and DCA services.

WealthManagement.com (trade press, 2026-09-11) reports that Merrill added a $1.2 billion UBS team in Santa Fe, N.M., producing about $4.7 million in revenue. It also reports that Merrill said earlier that week that advisors overseeing a combined $1.8 billion had joined from Morgan Stanley, Truist and Wells Fargo. The 2026-09-08 article details the Aliaskari Group ($1.2 billion from Morgan Stanley) and advisors from Truist (about $300 million) and Wells Fargo (about $285 million).

claims.text: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Borthwick said the Merrill 5% guide is to aim for 5% net new households growth over the next 3 to 5 years. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Borthwick said adviser attrition is 'near historic lows.' He also said Merrill and the Private Bank continued to attract talented advisers.

claims.text: Edward Jones defines its metric: the 2Q25 10-Q says "Attrition %" is the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period, compared with the total number of financial advisors at period end.

Edward Jones's 2Q25 10-Q (published August 2025) reports financial advisor attrition "increased to 6.4% primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends," with 20,309 financial advisors at quarter end.

Edward Jones's 3Q25 10-Q (published November 2025) reports financial advisor attrition of 6.1% "as a result of a variety of factors, including a rise in financial advisor departures with tenure of five years or less," with 20,429 financial advisors at quarter end.
The Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published March 2026) states the Partnership believes its rate of attrition of financial advisors is in line with comparable firms. It gives no figure for that comparison.

The Edward Jones 2025 10-K names attrition as a risk. It says attrition could increase with greater competition or lower profitability, and that there is no assurance past attrition rates will not rise.

Edward Jones's 2025 10-K reports financial advisors at year end of 20,425 (2025), 20,125 (2024) and 19,232 (2023), a 1% change for 2025. The year-end 2025 figure matches the 2024 figure only in the 1% change column; the three years are as printed.
Edward Jones's 2Q26 10-Q (published August 2026) shows 20,514 financial advisors at period end versus 20,309 a year earlier, up 1%.

The Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published March 2026) says it relies heavily on referrals from current financial advisors to recruit new advisors. It says recruiting has been harder in volatile markets, and that competitors offer guaranteed contracts, upfront payments and increased compensation.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Bank of America's CFO, discussing the Merrill growth goal, said "adviser attrition is now at near historic lows." This is a qualitative statement from management with no percentage given.

On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), Bank of America's CFO said the firm continued to add financial advisors in Merrill and the Private Bank through its training program and experienced hiring. He said approximately one-third of Q2 net new households were added by newly trained advisors.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), the CFO said Merrill advisors see the value of the franchise and the firm is "picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors," which he said is not an enormous part of the strategy.

On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), the CFO said the firm continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers. On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), he said Merrill and the Private Bank continued to attract talented advisers.

claims.text: On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CEO Ted Pick described the firm's advisor offering as including "compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating"; this is management's characterisation, and no payout rates were given.

The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that Wealth Management compensation and benefits expenses increased primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors, driven by higher compensable revenue. This shows advisor pay is formula-based and tied to compensable revenue; the formula itself is not given.

The 1Q26 10-Q (published 2026-05-05) says Wealth Management compensation and benefits expenses increased primarily from a higher formulaic payout to Wealth Management representatives, driven by higher compensable revenues. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) repeats this for advisors.
claims.source_label: MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-03-31 [filing]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: The 1Q26 10-Q (published 2026-05-05) states that deferred compensation for Wealth Management financial advisors is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards. The programs generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions.

The 1Q26 10-Q says employees may allocate the value of deferred cash-based awards among a menu of notional investments selected by the firm (fixed income, equity, commodity and money market funds). Compensation expense for these awards is based on the notional value granted, adjusted for changes in fair value of the referenced investments. It is recognised over the vesting period of each separately vesting portion.

The 2Q26 financial supplement (published 2026-07-15) says that beginning in 1Q26, hedges for Wealth Management deferred cash-based compensation (DCP) awards were primarily transitioned to derivatives. Changes in fair value are recorded in other comprehensive income and later reclassified to compensation expense over the vesting period for certain unvested awards, or recorded in compensation expense for other awards. As a result, the firm no longer presents non-GAAP measures excluding DCP.
In its 3Q26 earnings release (2026-10-14), Morgan Stanley said Wealth Management compensation expense increased from a year ago primarily driven by higher compensable revenues.

adjacent.text: The 4Q25 earnings release (2026-01-15) shows Wealth Management segment compensation expense of $16,950 million in FY 2025, against $15,207 million in FY 2024.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews (2026-10-26) reported that Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors must generate that much more revenue to see the same pay. It also reported that Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses in their 2027 pay plans.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews (2026-10-26) quoted recruiter Louis Diamond saying wirehouses tend to defer more of an advisor's pay. The article says large firms like Morgan Stanley have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation, with years of vesting required.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews (2026-11-10) reported on a FINRA arbitration in which Morgan Stanley sought to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans from an advisor. This indicates recruiting bonuses can take the form of loans.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative; it concerns one advisor's recruiting loans, not the general pay plan.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley: Payout grids are not public. The filings describe a "formulaic payout" to Wealth Management advisors but give no payout percentages, grid tiers, production thresholds, bonus amounts or average advisor pay.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley advisor compensation plan documents or recruiting materials, or industry compensation surveys (note these are not authoritative)
